name: requested_combine
why: The twin of `default_combine`. Same geometry, same outcome, and «union» is asked by name: the only difference between the two cases must be the declaration. We use «union» and not «subtract» on purpose — changing two things together (the value AND the outcome) would make the comparison useless, and on two bodies that do not touch it is not established that SOLIDWORKS accepts a subtraction that removes nothing. That is a question in its own right, and it must be measured when measuring, not assumed here. The two bodies OVERLAP on purpose — the copy is at 60 mm on a part 100 long, so 40 mm of overlap — because «combine_bodies» declares that it FAILS if after the union the bodies are still two: «they usually do not really touch, and I fail instead of confirming a part different from the one you believe». With two distant bodies the union would have failed and the red case would have accused the default instead of the geometry. With the overlap the three outcomes remain unmistakable: union = 80000 (50000+50000-20000), subtract = 30000, intersect = 20000. «succeeded: true» would give all three. And the bodies are indicated with «bodies_uid»: «move_bodies» does not declare it in «required» — it is an either/or between «bodies_uid» and «bodies_ref», which «required» cannot express — but its DESCRIPTION says so plainly. This case learned it by going red on 24/9/2026, and it is the second mistake of the same kind on the same case: written by looking at the schema instead of the description. *The schema says what an operation accepts; the description says what it demands and what it refuses.*

does_not_include: you have not asked for it
